dispatch_instance_contended.description: A policy admission found the instance's admission guard taken by a keyless observe or probe for its whole short retry (about 100 ms). The dispatch intent already written is rejected at info; the candidate may run again from next_eligible_unix_ms, about one second later.
dispatch_instance_contended.common_causes: A read-only observation or a monitor probe of the instance was in progress when the dispatch was admitted.
dispatch_instance_contended.handling: Nothing to repair. The next policy evaluation dispatches the candidate once the observation has finished.

dispatch_instance_cooldown.description: A policy candidate met an instance whose takeover cooldown still runs after a previous owner ended without closing; the candidate is deferred with a wake at next_eligible_unix_ms, the cooldown's end. Nothing is written for it.
dispatch_instance_cooldown.common_causes: actingd was killed or crashed while it held a lease on the instance, and the new owner started less than the takeover cooldown (6 s by default) ago.
dispatch_instance_cooldown.handling: Nothing to repair. The candidate is evaluated again when the cooldown ends.

dispatch_instance_held.description: A policy candidate, or its admission, met an instance that a claim holds or that an eligible claim waits for (holder_kind names the holder, or the waiting claim that receives the key next; count is the number of eligible waiting claims). The candidate is deferred with no wake, or its intent is rejected at info; the policy driver evaluates again when a lease is released, transferred or expires.
dispatch_instance_held.common_causes: A stuck-recovery ladder, a startup package, an operator command or a direct task run holds the instance, or waits for it, when a dispatch is due.
dispatch_instance_held.handling: Nothing to repair. The candidate runs after the holder releases the instance; actingctl status shows lease_active and queued_request_count meanwhile.

held_timeout.description: A held start (actingd --install-held) received no release before its held deadline. The installation transition fails with admission closed; the operation is install_transition.
held_timeout.common_causes: The installer stopped, timed out or lost its connection before it sent the release.

install_startup_shut_down.description: A held start (actingd --install-held) ended because a shutdown request for its owner was accepted before it was released; the operation is install_transition. It is a formal stop: the watchdog holds it and never restarts it.
install_startup_shut_down.common_causes: An installer, the console or actingctl request-shutdown stopped an owner that waited for its release.

install_startup_stopped.description: A held or released start stopped before it finished preparing because the Runtime latched a failure meanwhile; the operation is install_transition. The latched failure is the outcome's caused_by link in the ledger (ledger revision 3), and the tokens cause=<code> cause_operation=<operation> on the FATAL line and in the transition's status fact. A restart may succeed, so the watchdog considers a start.
install_startup_stopped.common_causes: A ledger write that failed on a request thread while the start was preparing.

maintenance_artifact_material_unavailabl.description: ledger-maintenance refused a root whose artifact retention is not settled: on a formal root an eviction intent without its outcome (pending_evictions counts the artifacts), on a Segment root any recorded eviction.
maintenance_artifact_material_unavailabl.common_causes: A hard stop (power loss, forced reboot) between an eviction intent and its outcome; a Segment root that already records evictions.
maintenance_artifact_material_unavailabl.handling: Start actingd once on the root so that startup recovery finishes the pending eviction, then run the maintenance operation again.

material_read_missing.description: A material read found no file for an artifact that has no eviction proof; the read result is missing and the Runtime records nothing.
material_read_missing.common_causes: A frame deleted by hand from the state root's artifacts folder.
material_read_missing.handling: Nothing to repair in the Runtime; the frame is gone. Read another frame, or restore the file from a copy if it is still needed.

policy_settlement_dispatch_unsettled.description: A start could not settle a scheduled run: the host's recovery or the ledger refused its settlement (failure_code is the refusal's code). The start carries on: the run's dispatch stays open, out of the active workloads, and the run's instance is paused with this code as the pause reason, so no new dispatch meets the open one. Recorded once per start, under the run's links, which carry the run id; lease_id is present when the dispatch has one lease grant.
policy_settlement_dispatch_unsettled.common_causes: A run whose recorded facts do not fit any settlement the Runtime knows, for example a ledger written by a defect in an earlier version.
policy_settlement_dispatch_unsettled.handling: Report it with the run id and failure_code: the open dispatch needs a fix in the Runtime. After looking, lift the instance's scheduling pause (resume scheduling for the instance) to let other tasks dispatch there again; the open dispatch itself stays open until a version that can settle it starts.

policy_settlement_release_recovered.description: A start found a scheduled run whose dispatch has no outcome and whose lease has no lease.released under its run links, wrote the missing release (effect not_performed) and settles the run once: from its terminal when it has one, otherwise as interrupted (policy_settlement_interrupted), so the dispatch is closed; the first such interruption of its pair in a row is lifted by the same start. Recorded once, under the run's links, which carry the run id.
policy_settlement_release_recovered.common_causes: The Runtime ended between a run's task terminal and its lease end (for example inside a failed run's hand-off to its stuck-recovery ladder), in the middle of a run (a reboot or a killed process), or after a scheduled dispatch's lease grant and before its run's first task event.
policy_settlement_release_recovered.handling: Nothing to repair: the run counts as its terminal says, or as interrupted when it has none. A second interruption of the same pair in a row keeps the pair paused until its package changes, as for any interrupted settlement.

policy_settlement_dispatch_left_open.description: After a start's reconciliation, a scheduled dispatch (its task's procedure is one the policy driver runs as a scheduled run) still has no outcome. The start settles every scheduled dispatch it can; this one stays open, and a later dispatch on its instance may be refused as a conflict. Recorded once per start, under the run's links, which carry the run id; lease_id is present when the dispatch has one lease grant.
policy_settlement_dispatch_left_open.common_causes: The run's instance is no longer in the configuration, or the run's lease ended in more than one way (for example two transfers).
policy_settlement_dispatch_left_open.handling: Report it with the run id: the open dispatch needs a fix in the Runtime. When the instance was removed from the configuration, adding it back lets the next start settle the run.

proposal_report_unavailable.description: A proposal or strategic report request was refused because a verified report artifact could not be read back: a proposal's cited report, or the stored report that a strategic report with identical content would reuse.
proposal_report_unavailable.common_causes: The report file was deleted by hand or damaged after it was recorded.
proposal_report_unavailable.handling: Restore the report file from a copy if it is still needed. Otherwise prepare a strategic report whose content differs (for example a later as-of position), which records a new report artifact, and cite that report.

recovery_ladder_key_lost.description: A stuck-recovery ladder found, at a holding check, that it no longer holds its instance's key. It cancels its continuation, records the current rung failed with this reason and finishes exhausted at warning, without an error point.
recovery_ladder_key_lost.common_causes: In practice only a stopping host; otherwise a step that overran its own bound so the key lapsed.
recovery_ladder_key_lost.handling: Nothing to repair: the instance is handed on, and the next trigger starts a new ladder.

release_timeout.description: A released start did not finish preparing before its release deadline. The installation transition fails with admission closed; the operation is install_transition.
release_timeout.common_causes: A slow preparation, such as the startup recovery of a long ledger.

strategic_evidence_unavailable.description: A strategic report request was refused because one of its verified evidence artifacts could not be read back.
strategic_evidence_unavailable.common_causes: An evidence frame or file was deleted by hand or damaged after it was recorded.
strategic_evidence_unavailable.handling: Cite evidence whose files still exist, then submit the report again.

frame_retention_remove_failed.description: The frame cleaner could not delete a due frame at its object key for another reason than a held or absent file. The frame stays, is not tried again by this process, and is tried again after a restart.
frame_retention_remove_failed.common_causes: Access to the state root's artifacts folder denied by the file system or by security software.
frame_retention_remove_failed.handling: Check the file's permissions and any program that blocks it, then restart actingd so that the cleaner tries again.

frame_retention_move_failed.description: The frame cleaner could not move an error or Lab frame into its kept folder (entry, relative to the state root) for another reason than a held or absent file; the frame stays at its object key, is not tried again by this process, and is tried again after a restart.
frame_retention_move_failed.common_causes: A file where the kept date folder or leaf should be; access to the state root's kept folder denied; a full disk.
frame_retention_move_failed.handling: Remove whatever blocks the kept folder named by entry, then restart actingd so that the cleaner tries again.

frame_retention_counter_failed.description: A frame moved into its kept folder, but the move counter kept/.moves (entry) could not be written, so other processes may find moved frames only at their next walk of the kept folders, within 60 s. Reported once per process.
frame_retention_counter_failed.common_causes: A folder or a read-only file where kept/.moves should be; access to the kept folder denied.
frame_retention_counter_failed.handling: Remove whatever occupies kept/.moves so that a file can be written there; the next move writes the counter again.

emulator_restart_stop_failed.description: An operator emulator restart (a Stop phase and then a Start phase under one instance admission guard) whose Stop was not confirmed: the provider's shutdown failed (stop_result names the device stage) or its readiness wait expired (stop_result wait_timeout). After an expired wait the Start phase still runs (start_dispatched true); after any other Stop failure it does not. The restart fails whatever its Start did, and the record carries the last observed state; it is the request's one failure record and its receipt terminal, written after the Start phase when one ran. The control failure behind it (emulator_control_wait_timeout or emulator_control_failed) is the outcome's caused_by link (ledger revision 3); stop_result is left out when the host's stop-result table gives the stage no token.
emulator_restart_stop_failed.common_causes: The vendor's shutdown of the instance hung, for example its device process stayed after Android stopped (device_process_present true), or MuMuManager refused the shutdown.

emulator_restart_start_failed.description: An operator emulator restart whose Stop phase was confirmed and whose Start phase failed: the provider's launch failed or its readiness wait expired. The state read after the failure is applied (a stopped instance is pending, with device.connected false) and carried on the record, which is the request's one failure record and its receipt terminal. The control failure behind it (emulator_control_wait_timeout or emulator_control_failed) is the outcome's caused_by link (ledger revision 3); stop_result is left out when the host's stop-result table gives the stage no token.
emulator_restart_start_failed.common_causes: The instance did not boot within the start's readiness wait, or MuMuManager refused the launch.

emulator_stop_process_unverified.description: A Stop was confirmed by MuMuManager info alone: the process listing that checks that no vendor device process of the instance is left failed or passed its bound, so device_process_present is unknown. Recorded once per Stop under the request's links (a stuck-recovery ladder's on its emulator-restart rung), before command.validated.
emulator_stop_process_unverified.common_causes: The process listing (PowerShell) did not answer within its bound under host load, or could not start.

clock_slot_refused.description: A persistent gate refused a due clock slot of a policy task on an instance (task_id, alias): a budget (policy_budget_exhausted, with budget_dimension), a closed activity window, a task paused by failure suspension, or the configuration (the task disabled for the instance, a missing capability or activity profile). gate_code is the gate's own code. Recorded once per task, instance and occurrence (occurrence_unix_ms) as a goal_missed planning signal whose outcome is this code with these values and whose signal_id is signal:clock_slot:refused:<sha256 of task, alias and occurrence>. window_end_unix_ms is the end of the activity window open at the refusal, next_eligible_unix_ms the first time the pair may be admitted again, next_occurrence_unix_ms the next clock occurrence.
clock_slot_refused.common_causes: A daily or window budget already used that day, often by an owed run that served the previous day's slot; the activity window closed before the slot could run; the task is paused after repeated failures; the task is disabled for the instance, or the instance lacks the operation or a matching activity profile.
clock_slot_refused.handling: Compare next_eligible_unix_ms with next_occurrence_unix_ms: below it, the slot runs later in the same or the next window; at or above it, the slot is lost to the next occurrence. Change the catalog (budget, slot times, activity window) or the instance configuration if the slot must run.

clock_slot_deferred.description: A transient gate held back a due clock slot of a policy task on an instance (task_id, alias). An operator scheduling pause is recorded at first sight; a queue wait (a held instance, a retry backoff, an activity interval or any other deferral) or an unavailable instance only at an evaluation where the pair's activity window is closed, that is once the wait outlasted the window. gate_code is the gate's own code. Recorded once per task, instance and occurrence as a goal_missed planning signal whose signal_id is signal:clock_slot:deferred:<sha256 of task, alias and occurrence>; it carries the same values as clock_slot_refused. A later refusal of the same occurrence because its window closed is not recorded.
clock_slot_deferred.common_causes: An operator paused scheduling across the slot; another claim held the instance until the activity window closed; the instance stayed unavailable until the window closed.
clock_slot_deferred.handling: Nothing to repair for an operator pause. For a wait that outlasted the window, check what held the instance (actingctl status) or why it stayed unavailable.

clock_slot_owed.description: A policy dispatch selected for a task on an instance (task_id, alias) serves a clock occurrence (occurrence_unix_ms) from before the activity window it was selected in opened (window_start_unix_ms); for a daily-limited task it uses the new day's budget for an earlier slot. first_run is true when the pair had no earlier dispatch; next_occurrence_unix_ms is the next clock occurrence, so a reader can tell whether the run still served this occurrence. Recorded once, at the first cycle that selects the pair for that occurrence, as a goal_missed planning signal whose signal_id is signal:clock_slot:owed:<sha256 of task, alias and occurrence>.
clock_slot_owed.common_causes: The slot fell while the activity window was closed or the Runtime was not running; a gate held the slot back the day before; a catalog was activated with new task ids outside the window.
clock_slot_owed.handling: Nothing to repair for a single owed run. Owed runs every morning together with refusals of the day's own slot mean that the slot's daily budget is displaced: gate the slot with its own timeline window or move it to the window start.

install_preparation_instance_unavailable.description: An install start (a held start released by the installer) went on although the daemon-start preparation self-check of this instance (instance_id) failed, because at least one other prepared instance passed (INST-1). The instance stays unavailable, as after a failed self-check at a normal start, until a later self-check passes; the other instances run. Recorded once per failed instance as a lifecycle record at stage install_release, linked to the transition's entered record. The self-check's failure is the outcome's caused_by link, for example input_backend_open_failed (ledger revision 3). When every prepared instance failed, the start ends as install_preparation_selfcheck_failed instead and this code is not recorded.
install_preparation_instance_unavailable.common_causes: The instance's device did not answer while the new build prepared it: its adb daemon hung or went offline, or the emulator or phone was stopped or unplugged.
install_preparation_instance_unavailable.handling: Bring the device back, then run actingctl selfcheck for the instance; a passing self-check makes it available again.

instance_resources_fenced.description: An unconfirmed close of one instance's own resources (instance_id) fenced that instance instead of ending the whole Runtime (Workflow #403). The fenced instance gets no new dispatch and its policy availability is withheld; its key goes only to the recovery ladder, and a person is needed once the ladder ended without proving the close (status resource_fence.awaiting_person). Recorded once when the instance is fenced, as a runtime.failed lifecycle record whose caused_by link is the unconfirmed failure (for example application_backend_operation_failed); the work that met the failure ends with this code, non-fatal, and a policy dispatch to the fenced instance is refused with it. Only a preparation whose self-check passes lifts the fence (instance_resources_fence_lifted). An unconfirmed failure that names no single instance still ends the whole Runtime.
instance_resources_fenced.common_causes: An application, input or capture backend of the instance did not confirm that its processes or handles ended: an adb command that hung while the emulator showed a black screen, a device that stopped answering in the middle of a close.
instance_resources_fenced.handling: Usually nothing: the recovery ladder restarts the application or the emulator and re-prepares the instance. When status shows the fence awaiting a person, bring the device back and run actingctl resume, an emulator restart or actingctl selfcheck for the instance; a passing self-check lifts the fence. If those are refused or keep failing, restart the Runtime: its start prepares and self-checks the instance again, and the other instances are not affected.

instance_resources_fence_lifted.description: A preparation of a fenced instance (instance_id) passed its self-check after the unconfirmed close, which proves the close: the resource fence is lifted, the instance's policy availability follows its self-check again and it schedules again (Workflow #403). Recorded once as the outcome of the resource_fence_lifted lifecycle record, which names the passing preparation's instance_preparation_finished record. The proving preparation is the recovery ladder's (after an application or emulator restart) or a person's resume, emulator start or restart, or self-check.
instance_resources_fence_lifted.common_causes: The recovery ladder restarted the application or the emulator and the instance's preparation passed, or a person resumed, restarted or self-checked the instance.

fact_reader_binding_invalid.description: Workflow #384 D2-S2: an instance's recognition maintenance package binding (instances[].recognition_package) is no reader: its package cannot be read (package_unreadable, caused by the loader's refusal), it does not qualify (designated_operation, no_marks, recognize_only, stability_termination), or one of its marks writes a key the configuration's policy.facts declares or a ledger_fact pool observes for the instance (policy_fact_authority, live_pool_key). check-config refuses the configuration; a Runtime start ignores the binding (fact_reader_binding_ignored).
fact_reader_binding_invalid.common_causes: acsetup or a hand edit bound a package that is not the standard package's recognition maintenance package, or the package changed.
fact_reader_binding_invalid.handling: Bind the standard package's recognition maintenance package, or fix the package or the configuration the reader_problem names.

fact_reader_binding_ignored.description: Workflow #384 D2-S2: a Runtime start found an instance's recognition package binding invalid (its caused_by link is fact_reader_binding_invalid) and runs without it; the start goes on. Recorded as a note link of the recognition_packages row of config.subsystems.
fact_reader_binding_ignored.common_causes: The bound package could not be read at the start, or its marks are claimed by policy.facts or a ledger_fact pool.
fact_reader_binding_ignored.handling: Run check-config for the full refusal and fix the binding; until then the instance has no reader.

fact_reader_missing.description: Workflow #384 D2-S2: the scheduler reads a realistic instance fact (resource.* or inventory.*; a catalog task's trigger or stop predicate in the instance's scope) that the instance's recognition maintenance package does not mark, or the instance has none. check-config warning; the configuration is still accepted.
fact_reader_missing.common_causes: The recognition maintenance package lacks a mark for the key, or no package is bound.
fact_reader_missing.handling: Add a mark for the key to the instance's recognition maintenance package, or bind one.

fact_reader_document_mismatch.description: Workflow #384 D2: a reading mark is looser than the scheduling-layer selection document that reads its key (confidence_below_document) or the reading interval exceeds the freshness it needs (interval_exceeds_freshness). check-config warning; emitted once actingd loads a scheduling-layer document (D2-S1 decision D3) and, for the interval, once D2-S4 reads scheduling.fact_refresh.min_interval_ms.

fact_adjustment_skipped.description: Workflow #384 D2-S3: a run confirmed an operation that declares a resource adjustment of fact_key, and the adjustment wrote nothing, for adjustment_reason. With after_read_missing (no reading of the key followed the confirmation) and amount_unresolved (the change the screen shows could not be read) the key's record is dropped, so the key is unknown until it is read again. task_id is the package's entry task. A task diagnostic row of the run, on its confirmation frame; the run itself succeeds.
fact_adjustment_skipped.common_causes: No reading mark of the key on a page the run passes after the operation, a mark or an amount that could not be read, a key with no current record, or an observation of the key already newer than the confirmation.
fact_adjustment_skipped.handling: Nothing to repair for base_missing, base_expired and newer_observation. For after_read_missing and amount_unresolved, check the package's marks and the amount's OCR target on the pages after the operation.

fact_adjustment_underflow.description: Workflow #384 D2-S3: a run's confirmed resource adjustment would take fact_key below zero: the change read on the confirmation frame is larger than the key's current value. Nothing is written and the key's record is dropped, so the key is unknown until it is read again. task_id is the package's entry task. A task diagnostic row of the run, on its confirmation frame; the run itself succeeds.
fact_adjustment_underflow.common_causes: The key's current record is stale or was misread, or the amount was misread.
fact_adjustment_underflow.handling: Check the key's reading mark and the amount's OCR target; the next reading of the key replaces the dropped record.

recovery_rung_skipped_no_startup_package.description: A stuck-recovery ladder skipped its application_restart rung: the instance has no startup package (the rung's recovery_rung_finished outcome; formerly the reason no_startup_package).

recovery_rung_skipped_no_emulator_contro.description: A stuck-recovery ladder skipped its emulator_restart rung: the instance has no emulator control (the rung's recovery_rung_finished outcome; formerly the reason no_emulator_control).

recovery_rung_skipped_capture_unavailabl.description: A stuck-recovery ladder skipped a rung because the instance's capture channel is known to be unavailable (the rung's recovery_rung_finished outcome; formerly the reason capture_unavailable).

recovery_rung_skipped_input_unavailable.description: A stuck-recovery ladder skipped a rung because the instance's input channel is known to be unavailable (the rung's recovery_rung_finished outcome; formerly the reason input_unavailable).

recovery_rung_skipped_adb_unavailable.description: A stuck-recovery ladder skipped a rung because the instance's ADB baseline does not answer (the rung's recovery_rung_finished outcome; formerly the reason adb_unavailable).

recovery_rung_skipped_resource_fence.description: A resource fence's stuck-recovery ladder skipped a rung that cannot prove the instance's close (the rung's recovery_rung_finished outcome; Workflow #403). The return-home rung only runs a package and never re-prepares the instance, so only the application restart and the emulator restart rungs can lift a fence.
recovery_rung_skipped_resource_fence.common_causes: An unconfirmed close fenced the instance and handed it to the ladder.

session_timeout.description: An agent session reached its deadline without a response: the Runtime answers it NeedsHuman with this code as the response code (formerly the unregistered spelling session_timeout).

recovery_ladder_exhausted.description: A stuck-recovery ladder ran out of rungs after the rungs that ran failed on their own (or every rung was skipped); the recovery_ladder_finished record's outcome, caused by the last failed rung's outcome when one failed.

recovery_ladder_interrupted.description: A holding interruption (shutdown, a lost key, an install drain, a closed admission, a pause drain or a key renewal refusal) ended a stuck-recovery ladder's climb; the outcome of the recovery_ladder_finished record and of the recovery_rung_finished record of the rung it ended, caused by the interruption.

channel_binding_missing.description: From #389 U-6 on, a connection that has not bound a channel with BindChannel sent a request other than the handshake (Health, BindChannel). The request is refused before the gate: the refusal is only in the receipt and nothing is written to the ledger. operation names the refused request kind. Until U-6 an unbound connection is bound from the source of its first request's envelope instead (contracts/runtime-interface.md, Channel binding).
channel_binding_missing.common_causes: A client built before #389 U-2, which never sends BindChannel; a client that skipped the handshake.
channel_binding_missing.handling: Use the Tools and the console of the same release as the Runtime: every current frontend binds its channel when it opens a connection.

channel_binding_exists.description: A connection sent BindChannel a second time. The connection keeps the channel it bound first, which channel names.
channel_binding_exists.common_causes: A client defect: the handshake ran twice on one connection.
channel_binding_exists.handling: Report the client defect. A client that needs another channel opens another connection.

channel_request_refused.description: From #389 U-6 on, the gate does not take this request kind on this channel: an option-one (authoring) or option-two (debugging) kind on a counter (cli, mcp, ui), a general instruction on the Lab channel, or an external approval on any channel. operation names the request kind and channel the connection's channel. A refused write, and a refused read that would have written a record, is copied by the ledger's request boundary (#383 G14) as command.rejected; a refused pure query is only in the receipt.
channel_request_refused.common_causes: A script sends a Lab operation through actingctl, MCP or the console; actinglab sends a pause, a monitor setting, a fact, a shutdown request or an upgrade-state request; any frontend sends an approval request, while approvals live in the configuration.
channel_request_refused.handling: Send general requests through actingctl, MCP or the console and Lab operations through actinglab; write approvals into the configuration.

lab_module_not_installed.description: From #389 U-6 on, the Lab channel sent a request other than the handshake while neither Lab option is installed (lab_module_authoring and lab_module_debugging both absent or false in the configuration the Runtime started with). The whole Lab channel is closed, general reads included. operation names the refused request kind.
lab_module_not_installed.common_causes: The installation was set up or upgraded without a Lab option; an actinglab.exe copied back by hand.
lab_module_not_installed.handling: Tick a Lab option on the installer's Lab page, or pass acsetup --lab; the Runtime reads the options at its next start.

lab_module_option_disabled.description: From #389 U-6 on, the Lab channel sent a request kind of a Lab option that is not installed while the other option is; lab_option names the missing option (authoring or debugging) and operation the request kind. The Lab channel stays open for the installed option.
lab_module_option_disabled.common_causes: Only one of the two Lab options was ticked in the installer.
lab_module_option_disabled.handling: Tick the other option on the installer's Lab page, or pass acsetup --lab; it takes effect at the next start.

upgrade_state_entered.description: UpgradeState enter succeeded (#389 U-4): the Runtime closed admission, drained, recorded its scheduling pause, accepted its own close while the requesting connection was still open, and closes with the upgrade-state marker on its owner-journal close record.
upgrade_state_entered.common_causes: acsetup entered the upgrade state before it replaces or restarts the Runtime.
upgrade_state_entered.handling: Nothing to repair. The installer goes on; if it fails after this point, the watchdog, when its task is registered, starts the selected generation again once the installer has released install\writer.lock.

upgrade_state_cancelled.description: UpgradeState cancel took effect while the transition was still draining: admission reopened, the transition is recorded as aborted and the Runtime keeps running.
upgrade_state_cancelled.common_causes: An interrupted installer run again, or a person or a script withdrew the upgrade.

upgrade_state_released.description: UpgradeState leave succeeded: the Runtime that acsetup started with --install-held prepared its provider, restored the pause recorded by the transition and opened admission.
upgrade_state_released.common_causes: acsetup released the Runtime it started held, after it checked the process id and the request id.

upgrade_state_requester_disconnected.description: The connection that sent UpgradeState enter closed before the Runtime accepted its own close. The Runtime handles it as cancel: admission reopens, the transition is recorded as aborted with this code as its failure_code, and the Runtime keeps running. No request receives this code as its reply.
upgrade_state_requester_disconnected.common_causes: The installer process ended or was killed while the Runtime was draining.
upgrade_state_requester_disconnected.handling: Run the installer again; the Runtime is unchanged and running.

upgrade_state_aborted.description: The reply to an UpgradeState enter that was still waiting for the drain when an UpgradeState cancel withdrew the transition. The Runtime keeps running.
upgrade_state_aborted.common_causes: A second installer run or a script sent cancel during the drain.
upgrade_state_aborted.handling: Nothing to repair; enter the upgrade state again when the upgrade should go on.

pack_registry_loaded.description: LoadPack succeeded (#389 U-3): the package, structurally admitted from its location, is in the Runtime's in-memory loaded-pack table, either restored from the start table or as a new or replacing binding. The change lasts until the Runtime restarts.
pack_registry_loaded.common_causes: A Lab debugging session loaded a package.

pack_registry_unloaded.description: UnloadPack completed (#389 U-3): the package left the in-memory loaded-pack table. Runs that used it were stopped through the same path as a run stop (scheduled runs, startup and ladder packages, prerequisite layers, and manual runs of the same package_id), its admitted but unstarted dispatches were withdrawn and its queued startup-package claims dropped. The result lists the stopped runs by request id and the withdrawn dispatches, and marks the runs still stopping when the wait ended. The change lasts until the Runtime restarts.
pack_registry_unloaded.common_causes: A Lab debugging session unloaded a package.
pack_registry_unloaded.handling: Nothing to repair. A restart loads the configuration's packages again.

pack_registry_entry_unknown.description: LoadPack restoring a start-table entry, or UnloadPack, named a package that is neither in the effective loaded-pack table nor in the configuration; the table is unchanged.
pack_registry_entry_unknown.common_causes: A mistyped package id; a package that the configuration does not bind.
pack_registry_entry_unknown.handling: Use a package id that the configuration binds or that a LoadPack in this Runtime epoch loaded.

pack_registry_entry_invalid.description: LoadPack replacing a start-table entry gave another run mode than the entry it replaces (scheduled_execution present on one side only, or another mode); the table is unchanged.
pack_registry_entry_invalid.common_causes: The replacing binding left out or changed scheduled_execution.
pack_registry_entry_invalid.handling: Give the replacing binding the entry's run mode. To change a run mode, change the configuration and restart the Runtime.

pack_registry_not_loaded.description: One of the Runtime's own requesters met a package that is not loaded: a policy candidate is deferred (before SR-11's pack_schedule_closed), a startup package or a ladder rung that needs it is skipped, a fact reader's dispatch is deferred, or a queued startup-package claim is dropped by an unload.
pack_registry_not_loaded.common_causes: The package was unloaded with UnloadPack in this Runtime epoch.
pack_registry_not_loaded.handling: Load the package again with LoadPack, or restart the Runtime to return to the configuration's packages.

pack_registry_dispatch_withdrawn.description: An unload withdrew a dispatch of the package that was admitted but had not started; recorded in the evaluation record and the reason chain.
pack_registry_dispatch_withdrawn.common_causes: The package was unloaded while one of its dispatches waited to start.

policy_rerun_owed.description: A rerun of a condition-terminated policy run (failure_code; count is its consecutive condition termination in this occurrence) is owed: the evaluator treats the pair as triggered and past its cooldown and promotes it ahead of the instance's other candidates. It is an ordinary policy dispatch in the instance's one queue.
policy_rerun_owed.common_causes: The previous run ended with a condition code (time too short, sampling timeout, blackout stop, performance yield or hold, entry-cost time check) and the condition has lifted.

policy_rerun_waiting.description: An owed rerun waits because the instance's pacing stage (pacing_stage) is above scheduling.rerun.resume_stage, or fell to it less than resume_settle_ms ago. It is evaluated again when the stage changes.
policy_rerun_waiting.common_causes: Host load keeps the instance at stage s3 or s4.
policy_rerun_waiting.handling: Nothing to repair; the rerun follows when the stage settles at or below the resume stage, or expires at the end of its bookkeeping window.

policy_rerun_expired.description: An owed rerun was not served before its bookkeeping window ended (window_end_unix_ms, taken from the settlement record). The run's failure then counts as an ordinary failure; the missed round is not carried into the next day.
policy_rerun_expired.common_causes: The condition (load or a blackout) lasted until the window ended.
policy_rerun_expired.handling: Nothing to repair for one occurrence. If it repeats, look at host load or the blackout table.

policy_rerun_exhausted.description: A pair ended with a condition code more often in one occurrence (count) than scheduling.rerun.max_per_occurrence allows (limit_count); that run settles as an ordinary recoverable failure, with no rerun.
policy_rerun_exhausted.common_causes: A package's time declarations are too tight even at stage s0.
policy_rerun_exhausted.handling: Look at the package's timeouts, sampling and entry-cost declarations.

pack_admission_suspended.description: A task package was suspended because admission refused it with a code of scheduling.pack_admission.suspend_codes (failure_code) under the Runtime build runtime_commit; actual_digest is the package's content hash measured after the refusal. Every task bound to the package, on every instance, is deferred with this code and never prepared again until the content hash or the build changes. Other task packages of the same standard package are unaffected; a standard package is never suspended as a whole.
pack_admission_suspended.common_causes: A package that needs more sampling time than its timeouts allow (recognition_sample_budget_invalid), typically after a Runtime upgrade with an unchanged package.
pack_admission_suspended.handling: Fix and replace the package; the suspension lifts when its content hash changes. A Runtime build that accepts it lifts it too.

pack_admission_lifted.description: A task package suspension was lifted because the package's content hash (actual_digest, as measured now) or the Runtime build (runtime_commit) changed. The next preparation tries the package once; the same refusal under the same content hash and build suspends it again.
pack_admission_lifted.common_causes: The package was replaced or the Runtime upgraded.

blackout_active.description: A candidate on the instance is deferred because a blackout (blackout_id: a catalog maintenance event or a host blackout entry) is active; it wakes at the blackout's end (next_eligible_unix_ms). Admission refuses an intent that crossed into the blackout with the same code.
blackout_active.common_causes: A configured maintenance or reset period, or a host blackout such as a planned machine restart.

blackout_approaching.description: A candidate is deferred because its response deadline (required_ms) plus the quiet margin would reach the next blackout's start (blackout_start_unix_ms); it wakes at that blackout's end. Shorter candidates still run, so the instance goes quiet gradually.

blackout_run_stopped.description: A run the Runtime started itself (a ladder rung, a startup package, or a policy run held by performance pacing) was still active when a blackout started and was stopped at its next checkpoint; its cancellation reason is BlackoutStop. A policy run settles as a condition termination and is rerun after the blackout. Client runs (direct and Lab runs) are never stopped this way.
blackout_run_stopped.common_causes: The blackout table changed after the run was admitted, or a ladder rung or startup package outlasted its estimate.
blackout_run_stopped.handling: Nothing to repair for one occurrence.

session_feature_fact_invalid.description: A session.feature. record breaks the feature-lock fact rules (its value is not a boolean, or it declares invalidate_on events); the publication request is refused. Not fatal.
session_feature_fact_invalid.common_causes: A client wrote a number or a text, or attached invalidation events.
session_feature_fact_invalid.handling: Publish a boolean record without invalidate_on.

due_task_missing.description: The instance has no task due in this evaluation; its not-running row names the earliest wake (next_eligible_unix_ms) when one is known.
due_task_missing.common_causes: Every task of the instance ran or waits for its next occurrence.

policy_cost_commit_waiting.description: A candidate whose task declares an entry-cost step (cost_commit) is deferred because the instance's pacing stage (pacing_stage) is above scheduling.cost_commit.max_stage; the instance's other candidates run as usual. It is evaluated again when the stage changes.
policy_cost_commit_waiting.common_causes: Host load keeps the instance at stage s3 or s4.

session_pack_schedule_invalid.description: A session.pack.schedule record breaks the pack schedule rules (field points at the offending member): its value is not a record_list of package_id, from_unix_ms, until_unix_ms and schedulable rows, a row ends at or before it starts, or two rows of one package overlap. The publication request is refused. Not fatal.
session_pack_schedule_invalid.common_causes: A client wrote overlapping periods for one package or swapped from and until.
session_pack_schedule_invalid.handling: Write the scope's whole list again with non-overlapping rows.

standard_pack_registered.description: A standard-pack game root's registry (package id to package directory, from bundle.json) was read at startup, or a run's preparation read a registry that differs from the one read before (Workflow #373 NAV-6): count is its number of packages; the added and removed package ids are listed, at most 64 each with their totals.

standard_pack_root_unreadable.description: A standard-pack game directory or root file, or the root directory itself (then without game), could not be read (an I/O failure other than a root file's absence; the OS error is the cause). Recorded at startup; a run that needs the root is refused in preparation (Workflow #373 NAV-6). A broken root never stops the Runtime.

contained_task_navigation_package_invali.description: A standard-pack package named for a part in a run (Workflow #373: the feature package, a shared interrupt page's handler or then.run package; NAV-5 adds edges and recovery chain steps) is not of the run's server, cannot be admitted (the loader's refusal is the cause) or is not eligible for the part. The run ends; data errors stop it (Fail Loud).

contained_task_interrupt_handled.description: A shared interrupt page was handled during a run (Workflow #373 NAV-6): its handler ran as a layer of the run, then its then.run package when it names one; count is how many times this run has handled the page. Carried by the interrupt_handled task record.

contained_task_interrupt_ambiguous.description: One frame matched two or more shared interrupt pages (Workflow #373 NAV-6): none was handled and the run went on as it would without them. Carried by the interrupt_ambiguous task record.

contained_task_interrupt_limit_reached.description: A shared interrupt page was seen once more than the run may handle it: its max_per_run, or 16 handlings of all pages in one run (Workflow #373 NAV-6). The run ends with no further input.

contained_task_interrupt_escalated.description: A shared interrupt page whose then is end_run was handled (Workflow #373 NAV-6): the run ends after its handler, as the standard pack's data asks; the ladder configuration decides what follows a routine run.

host_config_overrides_fact_invalid.description: At start the recorded host.config_overrides fact is not of the shape this build writes; the start fails, and every later start until the ledger is repaired.
host_config_overrides_fact_invalid.common_causes: A ledger written by another build.
host_config_overrides_fact_invalid.handling: Restore a ledger this build wrote, or move the state root aside.

host_config_overrides_persist_failed.description: A ConfigureSettings change could not record host.config_overrides; nothing changed and the request is refused (caused_by: the ledger's refusal).
host_config_overrides_persist_failed.common_causes: The ledger refused the record, for example at its capacity bound.
host_config_overrides_persist_failed.handling: Read the ledger state, then send the change again.

host_config_overrides_fact_clock_overflo.description: A configuration fact cannot be recorded after the previous one: its observation time would overflow.

host_config_value_type_invalid.description: A value the configuration in effect holds, or an identity a configuration record needs, is not of the type the reader expects (an internal invariant).

performance_event_rejected.description: A performance observation event that contract sanitization refused was dropped, and the performance monitor degraded instead of ending the Runtime; the refusal is the caused_by link.

runtime_receipt_build_failed.description: The Runtime host could not build the runtime receipt of a request; the host latches the failure (was the runtime client's runtime_receipt_invalid, which names a receipt the client cannot read).

planning_fact_unknown.description: A policy candidate's predicate read a fact (fact_key) that is unknown (unknown_reason), and the policy reserves a detection for it: the outcome of a detection_reserved or detection_quota_exhausted planning signal.

strategic_feasibility_red.description: A strategic report finds a goal infeasible on an instance at best effort: the outcome of a feasibility_red planning signal.

strategic_timeline_reached.description: A strategic report finds a goal's deadline reached on an instance with a shortfall left: the outcome of a timeline_reached planning signal.

policy_instance_fact_missing.description: A policy evaluation found no usable instance fact (fact_key) for an instance and projected the instance unavailable.

priority_offset_unknown_task.description: A priority offset names a task (task_id) the active catalog does not declare; the offset is ignored.

policy_detection_reason_unknown.description: A policy evaluation's detection suggestion carries a reason that the unknown_reason vocabulary does not list, so its planning signal cannot be recorded.

recovery_rung_skipped_before_start_rung.description: A stuck-recovery ladder skipped a rung before the start rung its trigger item names (the rung's recovery_rung_finished outcome; Workflow #387 D1c, recovery_ladder.triggers[].start_rung or trigger_defaults.start_rung).
recovery_rung_skipped_before_start_rung.common_causes: A trigger item, or the trigger defaults, start the climb at a later rung.
recovery_rung_skipped_before_start_rung.handling: Nothing to do; change the trigger item's start_rung to climb from an earlier rung.

recovery_rung_skipped_device_not_ready.description: A stuck-recovery ladder skipped a rung whose entry the device-state gate holds: a locked screen, heat, a low battery or a device in use (the rung's recovery_rung_finished outcome; skip reason device_not_ready, Workflow #398 M398 section 6.4, registered with Workflow #387 D1c; the device-state slice emits it).

contained_task_navigation_recovery_exhau.description: A run's navigation recovery chain ran out without reaching its entry page (count is the number of steps run; caused by the last locate's code; Workflow #373 M-373 sections 5 and 9). Registered with Workflow #387 D1c for its default trigger item navigation_exhausted; NAV-5 emits it.
contained_task_navigation_recovery_exhau.common_causes: The game shows a page the standard pack's navigation data cannot leave, or its recovery chain is too short.
contained_task_navigation_recovery_exhau.handling: The recovery ladder's trigger item navigation_exhausted starts at the emulator restart rung by default; check the standard pack's navigation data if it recurs.

perf_run_yielded.description: Performance pacing ended a policy run to be rerun: it reached its wall-clock ceiling after pacing lengthened it (yield_cause wall_ceiling) or was preempted while held (preempted). Its cancellation reason is PerformanceYield; the run settles as a condition termination and is owed a rerun (Workflow #385 PERF §7.4). Registered by SH-1; P-k and P-h emit it.
perf_run_yielded.common_causes: The host stayed slow long enough for a lengthened run to reach its ceiling, or the instance was paused by its share while the run was held.
perf_run_yielded.handling: Nothing to repair for one occurrence; the run is rerun.

perf_hold_expired.description: A policy run was held at its pace checkpoint longer than the hold limit (timeout_ms) and ended; its cancellation reason is PerformanceYield, it is owed a rerun, and the recovery ladder may start once performance releases the instance (Workflow #385 PERF §7.4, M387 §3.7). Registered by SH-1; P-h emits it.
perf_hold_expired.common_causes: The host stayed in the deepest pacing stage longer than the hold limit.
perf_hold_expired.handling: Nothing to repair for one occurrence; the run is rerun.

input_action_unsupported.description: An input request names an action this build decodes but does not perform: the single-touch path drag (InputAction::SingleTouchPathDragV1) is reserved until Workflow #406 T-3. The request is refused before any effect; nothing reaches the device.
input_action_unsupported.common_causes: A client built for a later Runtime sent the path drag to this build.
input_action_unsupported.handling: Send the action to a Runtime that performs it, or use a supported input action.
